# `Q-20-3` — Pandoc Exited With An Error

> The `pandoc` subprocess exited with a nonzero status. Its stderr is
> reproduced verbatim below, including any Lua filter traceback.

## What this means

Quarto shelled out to `pandoc` to produce this document, and the `pandoc`
process itself failed — it did not exit successfully, so no output file was
written. Quarto reproduces the pandoc process's own stderr output verbatim
in this diagnostic, because that text (often a Lua stack traceback) is the
most direct description of what actually went wrong.

## Why this happens

- A Lua filter crashed while processing the document — the traceback in the
  stderr text usually names the failing filter file and line.
- The document's Pandoc-JSON representation is malformed in a way pandoc's
  reader rejects.
- A required filter parameter was missing or malformed, and a Lua filter
  indexed it unconditionally.

## How to fix

Read the reproduced stderr text closely — it names the failing Lua file and
line, which usually identifies the cause directly. If the traceback points
into Quarto's own vendored filter tree rather than your document, this is
likely a Quarto bug; please file an issue with the full diagnostic text.

## Related errors

- [`Q-20-4`](Q-20-4.qmd) — a specific cause of a nonzero pandoc exit: the
  filter params payload exceeded a platform limit before pandoc even ran.
